I know it's a contrived scenario but I think it gets the point across.
I want to author an addition to mise, in the form of a new command mise vendor (or a sub-command under mise generate). The rough idea is that mise vendor will take the packages in your mise.lock and will download the installation sources (i.e .tar.gz etc) from whatever backend the tool comes from, and save it locally. Then users may back up the vendored directory however they see fit.
When restoring from a vendored backup, mise will use the local vendored sources to install the tools it is requesting, and will seamlessly switch back over to using whatever original remote backend the tools actually came from when updating the tool.
Necessary changes:

Add the mise vendor command

Download installation sources and save them locally
Manifest of local vendored sources & hashes for provenance,verification & other security concerns


extend mise generate bootstrap to allow the mise bootstrap script to use a local archive of mise, instead of downloading from github

mise vendor will use it to vendor mise itself


a vendored backend which will report that it provides the vendored tools at their specific revision, with a high priority so that install/use will first use the vendored backend before trying any other backends.

Or a mise vendor restore (name TBD) command that acts as the only way to use the aforementioned vendored backend.
I'm pretty sure I can implement this backend as a backend plugin in Lua, which I will do as a Proof of Concept



I'm not super attached to the proposed names of commands/things I gave in this summary, they names are just to communicate the idea and the concepts used, that is to say I'm happy to take suggestions or directives about names."},{"number":12719,"title":"Zsh completion for `mise plugins uninstall` only lists core plugins","url":"https://github.com/jdx/mise/discussions/12719","updatedAt":"2026-09-03T21:44:26Z","bodyText":"$ mise plugin

A task with sources globs and cache = { enabled = true } hashes its sources by expanding the glob. The ** expansion follows symlinks and has no loop detection. On a tree that links back into itself, mise allocates until it is killed and the task command never runs.
Reproduction steps:
[settings]
experimental = true

# Two links are the smallest trigger, because the Linux kernel stops a single loop at 40 levels (ELOOP).
[tasks.make-loop-tree]
description = "Sets up 2 sym links in a loop."
run = "mkdir -p tree && ln -sfn . tree/a && ln -sfn . tree/b"

[tasks.cached-task]
depends = ["make-loop-tree"]
run = "true"
sources = ["tree/**/*"]
outputs = []
cache = { enabled = true }

[tasks.cached-task-watched]
description = "Runs cached-task in the background, prints its memory usage once a second, and kills it past MEMORY_LIMIT_MB."
quiet = true
run = """
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -u

memory_limit_mb=${MEMORY_LIMIT_MB:-1024}
timeout_seconds=60

mise run cached-task &
mise_pid=$!

elapsed_seconds=0
while kill -0 "$mise_pid" 2>/dev/null && [ "$elapsed_seconds" -lt "$timeout_seconds" ]; do
  sleep 1
  elapsed_seconds=$((elapsed_seconds + 1))

  rss_kb=$(ps -o rss= -p "$mise_pid" 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' ')
  rss_mb=$(( ${rss_kb:-0} / 1024 ))
  echo "after ${elapsed_seconds}s: mise is using ${rss_mb} MB"

  if [ "$rss_mb" -gt "$memory_limit_mb" ]; then
    kill -9 "$mise_pid"
    echo "killed mise at ${rss_mb} MB. The task command never ran."
    exit 1
  fi
done

wait "$mise_pid"
"""

Save mise.toml in an empty directory, then:
mise trust && mise run cached-task-watched

Without the watched command, mise run cached-task, grows by 50 to 100 MB per second until the OS kills it.

I ran into this issue when I added test fixtures to my application for reading hardware sensors on Linux. sysfs links each device to its class in both directions: class/hwmon/hwmon0 points at the device directory, and the device's subsystem points back at class/hwmon."},{"number":12690,"title":"Lazy tools do not work on Windows","url":"https://github.com/jdx/mise/discussions/12690","updatedAt":"2026-09-02T15:11:35Z","bodyText":"Using mise version 2026.09.0 on Windows.

node.compile = false"},{"number":12659,"title":"`[env] VAR = false` does not unset a variable inherited from the process environment","url":"https://github.com/jdx/mise/discussions/12659","updatedAt":"2026-09-02T15:08:33Z","bodyText":"Summary
The docs state that setting an env var to
false clears it:
[env]
NODE_ENV = false # unset a previously set NODE_ENV
In practice false only cancels an assignment made by an earlier mise config
file. If the variable already exists in the process environment when mise runs,
it survives untouched and leaks into mise exec, mise run, mise env and
activated shells.
The same docs page establishes that mise reasons about this state elsewhere — the
default directive is described as keeping a value "if it was already set
before mise ran or by an earlier config file" — so false failing to reach
the pre-existing case reads as a bug rather than intended scoping.
Reproduction
A single mise.toml, nothing else:
[env]
FOO = false
$ mise exec -- sh -c 'echo ${FOO-<absent>}'
<absent>                # correct

$ FOO=leaked mise exec -- sh -c 'echo ${FOO-<absent>}'
leaked                  # BUG: expected <absent>
${FOO-<absent>} is deliberate — plain $FOO cannot distinguish "set to the
empty string" from "genuinely unset", which is what made this hard to spot.
Reproduced in a fully clean environment, with mise never activated, to rule out
any session state:
$ env -i HOME="$HOME" PATH=/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin FOO=leaked \
      /usr/local/bin/mise -C /tmp/repro exec -- sh -c 'echo FOO=[${FOO-<absent>}]'
FOO=[leaked]
Affected surfaces
Every surface leaks. The commands below use a slightly larger config than the one
above: a profile, plus a second variable as a control, plus a task.
# mise.toml
[env]
SET_ENV = 'set'
UNSET_ENV = 'unset'

[tasks]
check = "echo SET_ENV=[${SET_ENV-<absent>}] UNSET_ENV=[${UNSET_ENV-<absent>}]"
# mise.dev.toml
[env]
UNSET_ENV = false
SET_ENV = 'dev'
$ mise run check
SET_ENV=[set] UNSET_ENV=[unset]

$ MISE_ENV=dev mise run check
SET_ENV=[dev] UNSET_ENV=[<absent>]              # correct

$ UNSET_ENV=from_parent MISE_ENV=dev mise run check
SET_ENV=[dev] UNSET_ENV=[from_parent]           # BUG
With UNSET_ENV=from_parent MISE_ENV=dev:



Surface
Result
Expected




mise exec -- sh -c 'echo ${UNSET_ENV-<absent>}'
from_parent
<absent>


mise run check
from_parent
<absent>


mise env -s bash
no unset line emitted
unset UNSET_ENV


mise env --json
key absent from output
n/a (cannot express an unset)


mise activate bash + _mise_hook
from_parent
<absent>


mise hook-env -s bash
UNSET_ENV not mentioned
unset UNSET_ENV



Note the SET_ENV control in the same runs: overriding a pre-existing value with
a string works correctly (from_parent → dev). Only the false / unset path
fails.
The activated-shell row, from a clean shell:
$ env -i HOME="$HOME" PATH=/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin \
      UNSET_ENV=from_parent MISE_ENV=dev \
      bash --noprofile --norc -c '
        eval "$(mise activate bash)"
        cd /path/to/repro
        _mise_hook
        echo "UNSET_ENV=[${UNSET_ENV-<absent>}] SET_ENV=[${SET_ENV-<absent>}]"'
UNSET_ENV=[from_parent] SET_ENV=[dev]
Why this matters in practice: with mise activate in a shell rc, or in CI, or
simply after having run once in a non-dev profile in the same shell, the
variable is already exported before mise evaluates the config — so the false
never takes effect in exactly the situation it is meant for.
Not a duplicate of #12090 / #12389
Both of those concern __MISE_DIFF / prompt-hook session state overriding
values. This is a different mechanism, and the false/unset path is broken
even with that state absent:
$ UNSET_ENV=from_parent MISE_ENV=dev env -u __MISE_DIFF mise exec -- \
      sh -c 'echo [${UNSET_ENV-<absent>}]'
[from_parent]
Also reproduces with __MISE_DIFF never set at all, mise never activated, a
single config file, and no profiles (see the clean-env command above). Plain
string assignment works fine here, whereas in #12389 plain assignment is the case
that works and templates/default are the ones that break — the opposite split.
Root cause analysis
Against main @ c6f6130a03205ee1f9b63142244a8ebff4d1e918.
EnvDirective::Rm records the key in EnvResults.env_remove and drops it from
the in-progress overlay map:
// src/config/env_directive/mod.rs:615-630
EnvDirective::Rm(k, _opts) => {
    ...
    env.shift_remove(&k);
    ...
    r.env_remove.insert(k);
}
Every consumer of env_remove then performs only a map removal:

src/task/mod.rs:2409 — for key in &results.env_remove { env.remove(key); }
src/task/task_context_builder.rs:454 — same
src/config/config_file/mise_toml.rs:1482 — same
src/toolset/toolset_env.rs — final_env() / env_with_path() return
EnvResults but never apply env_remove themselves
src/cli/exec.rs:223 — let mut env = ts.env_with_path(&config).await?; then
cmd.envs(env); env_remove is never consulted
src/cli/env.rs:191 — iterates the set-map calling shell.set_env(k, v);
shell.unset_env is never called

That map is additive: it is layered on top of the inherited environment via
Command::envs, or printed as export lines. Deleting a key from an additive
overlay is a no-op with respect to the parent's value, so env_remove never
becomes a real unset.
The primitives already exist and are used elsewhere in the codebase:

Cmd::env_remove (src/cmd.rs:668) → std::process::Command::env_remove
Shell::unset_env, and EnvDiffOperation::Remove (src/env_diff.rs:34), used
by hook-env / deactivate — #12090 shows hook-env emitting unset MY_VAR,
so the shell-level unset path is reachable, just not wired to env_remove

So the fix looks like plumbing rather than new machinery: apply
env_results.env_remove via Command::env_remove on the exec/run paths, and emit
shell.unset_env(k) for each env_remove key in mise env / hook-env.
Expected behaviour
VAR = false should unset VAR regardless of whether the value came from an
earlier mise config file or from the environment mise was invoked in — matching
the documented "unset a previously set NODE_ENV".
If the current behaviour is intentional and false is only ever meant to cancel
mise-config assignments, the docs should say so explicitly, and there should be a
documented way to unset an inherited variable.
mise doctor

The reported warnings/problems are unrelated to this bug and reproduce without
them.

one of the things I'm trying to get rid of is node and npm.
There appears to have been some prior work on creating a standalone bun: backend in #2899, which was (sensibly) folded into
the existing npm backend as npm.package_manager = "bun" — matching the pipx/uv pattern. That works great for installing
packages with bun, but it doesn't actually let me drop node/npm from the system: the npm backend still shells out to npm
view for version listing and latest resolution, regardless of which package manager performs the install. The two TODOs at
src/backend/npm.rs:209 and :577 reference exactly this gap.
The blocker called out at the time was that bun view / bun pm view didn't exist (oven-sh/bun#1224). That has since changed -
bun pm view shipped in Bun 1.2.15 (oven-sh/bun#19841), and @risu729 already flagged this on the original PR thread, with
the caveat that switching unconditionally would force every existing npm.package_manager = "bun" user onto a recent bun.
Before I start writing any code, I wanted to check whether you'd be open to a change along these lines, and get your input
on a few scoping questions:

Approach. I'm assuming you'd still prefer this to live inside src/backend/npm.rs rather than as a new bun: backend,
consistent with the #2899 decision. Concretely: when npm.package_manager resolves to bun and the installed bun is new
enough, route _list_remote_versions and latest_stable_version through bun pm view and drop node/npm from get_dependencies /
ensure_npm_for_version_check on that path. Older bun would keep using npm view. Does that shape match what you'd want?
Minimum bun version. bun pm view first shipped in 1.2.15. I'd plan to gate via a version probe analogous to
npm_supports_min_release_age_flag (read from the toolset when bun is mise-managed, fall back to bun --version), and document
the minimum in docs/dev-tools/backends/npm.md. Happy to use a higher minimum if there are known bugs in early versions.
Custom registries. The original PR explicitly kept npm view for custom-registry support. I'll verify whether bun pm view
honors NPM_CONFIG_REGISTRY / project-level .npmrc before sending a PR. If it doesn't, the npm-view fallback would need to
stay for users with custom registry configuration — would you want that controlled by an additional setting, or is "use bun
pm view only when no custom registry is configured" sufficient?
Opt-in vs. transparent. Should the node-free path activate automatically whenever bun is the active package manager and
bun pm view is available, or behind an explicit opt-in (e.g. npm.bun_node_free = true) so existing users on older bun don't
see behaviour changes? My preference would be transparent with a version gate, but I'll defer to you here.

Happy to open a draft PR once there's some direction on the above. If this is out of scope or you'd rather it wait, just say
the word and I'll leave it alone."},{"number":12238,"title":"[BUG] Case of `mise run --output keep-order` remove the outputs","url":"https://github.com/jdx/mise/discussions/12238","updatedAt":"2026-09-01T23:16:55Z","bodyText":"References

At 2026-08-28T09:56:38Z, minimum_release_age = "24h" caused Codex resolution to skip eligible 0.150.0 and report 0.149.1 as the latest eligible release.
This looks like a mismatch between the shared mise-versions list and the canonical latest-release metadata, rather than a duration-calculation error.
Observed data
GitHub reports:



Release
GitHub published_at




rust-v0.150.0
2026-08-26T19:37:28Z


rust-v0.150.1
2026-08-27T01:56:54Z



At the observation time, 0.150.0 was more than 24 hours old. The upstream Aqua/GitHub version listing contained both 0.150.0 and 0.150.1.
However, the hosted list at https://mise-versions.jdx.dev/codex.toml contained 0.149.1, but no stable 0.150.0 or 0.150.1 entry.
That produces an inconsistent result: the canonical-latest path sees 0.150.1 and correctly excludes it as too new, while the release-age-filtered version-list path cannot see 0.150.0 and falls back to 0.149.1.
Reproduction
$ mise ls-remote codex --minimum-release-age 24h --json
# stable candidate was 0.149.1; 0.150.0 was absent

$ MISE_USE_VERSIONS_HOST=0 MISE_FETCH_REMOTE_VERSIONS_CACHE=0 mise ls-remote codex --minimum-release-age 24h --json
# includes 0.150.0 as the newest eligible stable release
The user-facing symptom from mise update was:
mise WARN newer codex release 0.150.1 ignored by minimum_release_age (24h); latest eligible release is 0.149.1

Possible directions
The smallest fix may be to improve or investigate Codex ingestion/update cadence for mise-versions; it is a cache and temporary lag may be expected.
I also prototyped a client-side safeguard, not a proposed PR yet: when canonical latest metadata says the newest stable release is too new for the cutoff, fetch the backend's upstream version list before choosing the prior eligible release. That avoids choosing an older release solely because the shared list has not caught up, but adds an upstream request in this edge case.
Would maintainers prefer treating the hosted list as authoritative during its normal lag window, or is a direct fallback appropriate specifically for release-age resolution?
AI-assisted — Tool: Codex; model: unavailable; version: unavailable."},{"number":12684,"title":"brew-cask: only the declared artifacts are installed, so codex loses the sibling host it execs","url":"https://github.com/jdx/mise/discussions/12684","updatedAt":"2026-09-01T19:56:27Z","bodyText":"Another brew-cask one. "brew-cask:codex" = "latest" installs cleanly and codex --version reports 0.152.0, but every tool call fails, because the cask ships more than the one binary it declares and only that binary survives the install.
The cask declares a single artifact:
binary "bin/codex"
generate_completions_from_executable "bin/codex", "completion"
while codex-package-aarch64-apple-darwin.tar.gz (sha256 5287a514213f8134210677cce51b23e2eaeaff1925362f18318e4268a5ab1d1b) contains five paths:
bin/codex
bin/codex-code-mode-host
codex-package.json
codex-path/rg
codex-resources/zsh/bin/zsh

Afterwards the Caskroom directory holds the declared binary and the generated completions, and nothing else:
/opt/homebrew/Caskroom/codex/0.152.0/
├── .mise-cask.toml
├── bin/codex
├── etc/bash_completion.d/codex
└── share/…

codex-package.json is the manifest the binary reads to find the rest of its own layout, so losing it costs more than the file itself:
{
  "layoutVersion": 1,
  "version": "0.152.0",
  "entrypoint": "bin/codex",
  "resourcesDir": "codex-resources",
  "pathDir": "codex-path"
}
Codex 0.152.0 runs every tool call through a codex-code-mode-host subprocess. With no host beside the binary it falls back to whatever other copy is on the machine — here the 0.151.0-alpha.7.1 host bundled inside ChatGPT.app — and every command, down to /usr/bin/true, dies before dispatch:
failed to read code-mode host message: failed to decode code-mode IPC frame: missing field `code_mode_host_duration_ns`

The older host never emits that field and the 0.152.0 decoder requires it, so nothing looks wrong until an upgrade moves the CLI ahead of the stale host. Extracting the four missing paths back into the Caskroom directory fixed it here with no other change, which is what points at the install rather than at Codex.
I take the Homebrew behaviour to be staging the whole extracted payload in the Caskroom and symlinking only the declared artifacts out of it, which leaves the siblings where the binary expects them. I can't confirm that side by side — this machine has no Homebrew, which is rather the point of installing casks through mise.
Any cask whose binary resolves resources relative to itself would hit this, so it seemed worth reporting past the one package. Happy to re-run with MISE_VERBOSE=1 and attach output.

Author: Jeff Dickey <@jdx>"},{"number":12621,"title":"`mise.lock` loses `provenance_verified` on every install that doesn't re-verify provenance","url":"https://github.com/jdx/mise/discussions/12621","updatedAt":"2026-09-01T13:50:05Z","bodyText":"Summary
mise install rewrites mise.lock, deleting provenance_verified = true for any tool whose
provenance was not verified in that run — including for platforms.* entries the current run
isn't installing at all.
The field is committed by whoever runs mise install on a machine that does verify (a dev laptop),
then stripped by a machine that doesn't (a Linux CI runner), so the lockfile flip-flops and every
CI job leaves a dirty working tree.
Environment

mise 2026.7.7 linux-x64 (2026-07-15), Alpine/musl, linux/amd64 (GitLab CI). Not re-tested
on 2026.8.x — we are pinned to 2026.7.7 by a separate npm: backend regression.
mise.toml: experimental = true, lockfile = true, minimum_release_age = "3d"

mise doctor
From the same CI job that produced the diff below (paths elided, tool list trimmed to the
github: backend tools involved):
version: 2026.7.7 linux-x64 (2026-07-15)
activated: no
shims_on_path: no

build_info:
  Target: x86_64-unknown-linux-musl
  Features: openssl, rustls-native-roots, self_update
  Built: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 18:02:28 +0000
  Rust Version: rustc 1.94.0 (4a4ef493e 2026-03-02)
  Profile: release

shell:
  bash
  GNU bash, version 5.3.9(1)-release (x86_64-alpine-linux-musl)

dirs:
  cache: ~/.cache/mise
  config: ~/.config/mise
  data: $CI_PROJECT_DIR/.mise-data
  shims: $CI_PROJECT_DIR/.mise-data/shims
  state: ~/.local/state/mise

toolset:
  github:jdx/fnox@1.26.0
  github:lucagrulla/cw@4.1.3
  … (plus core:, aqua:, npm: and pipx: tools)

env_vars:
  MISE_DATA_DIR=$CI_PROJECT_DIR/.mise-data

settings:
  all_compile          false ~/.config/mise/config.toml
  experimental         true  $CI_PROJECT_DIR/mise.toml
  lockfile             true  $CI_PROJECT_DIR/mise.toml
  minimum_release_age  "3d"  $CI_PROJECT_DIR/mise.toml

1 problem found:
1. mise is not activated … (tasks get tool dirs injected, so this is expected here)

Reproduction

Have a committed mise.lock in which a github:-backend tool whose releases carry
attestations (github:jdx/fnox@1.26.0 here) records, per platform — i.e. written by a machine
that did verify; ours has entries for both linux and macOS platforms:
[tools.fnox."platforms.linux-x64"]
checksum = "sha256:…"
url = "https://github.com/jdx/fnox/releases/download/v1.26.0/fnox-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz"
url_api = "https://api.github.com/repos/jdx/fnox/releases/assets/445847496"
provenance = "github-attestations"
provenance_verified = true

Commit mise.lock.
On a Linux CI runner, fresh checkout, mise install.
git diff is non-empty:

--- a/mise.lock
+++ b/mise.lock
@@ -146,14 +146,12 @@
  url = "https://github.com/jdx/fnox/releases/download/v1.26.0/fnox-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz"
  url_api = "https://api.github.com/repos/jdx/fnox/releases/assets/445847496"
  provenance = "github-attestations"
-provenance_verified = true

  [tools.fnox."platforms.macos-arm64"]
  checksum = "sha256:65295b6cf9a345240967f3fd73db4645d7e4ec3ef4f20f735bd41802c92896f7"
  url = "https://github.com/jdx/fnox/releases/download/v1.26.0/fnox-aarch64-apple-darwin.tar.gz"
  url_api = "https://api.github.com/repos/jdx/fnox/releases/assets/445847391"
  provenance = "github-attestations"
-provenance_verified = true
Note the second entry is platforms.macos-arm64, which a linux-x64 runner never installs.
provenance = "github-attestations" is retained in both; only provenance_verified goes.
Why that run didn't verify
In the same install, another github:-backend tool was verified, while fnox was only checksummed:
mise github:lucagrulla/cw@4.1.3 [2/3] verify GitHub artifact attestations
mise github:lucagrulla/cw@4.1.3 [2/3] verify SLSA provenance
mise github:lucagrulla/cw@4.1.3 [3/3] extract cw_4.1.3_Linux_x86_64.tar.gz

mise fnox@1.26.0 [1/3] download fnox-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz
mise fnox@1.26.0 [2/3] checksum fnox-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz
mise fnox@1.26.0 [3/3] extract fnox-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz
mise fnox@1.26.0 ✓ installed

so the difference in behaviour between the two tools may be part of the same story. The same run
also logs, before any of the above:
mise WARN  lockfile asset 'biome-linux-x64-musl' doesn't match registry, refreshing
mise WARN  lockfile asset 'pnpm-linux-x64-musl.tar.gz' doesn't match registry, refreshing

Expected
mise.lock should be stable across machines:

don't rewrite platforms.* entries the current run isn't installing;
for the platform being installed, either re-verify and keep the field, or leave a previously
recorded provenance_verified alone rather than deleting it.

Impact
Every CI job dirties the working tree, so a "generated files are committed" or "lockfile is clean"
check can't distinguish this from real drift, and committing mise.lock from either machine
reverses the other.
Related
Unrelated to #12620 (npm: tools unresolvable inside a pnpm workspace) beyond both showing up in
the same pipeline — that one is why we are pinned to 2026.7.7 here.
Question
Is provenance_verified intended to record "this artifact's provenance has been verified at some
point" (persistent) or "…was verified during this run" (ephemeral)? If the latter, it probably
shouldn't be in the committed lockfile at all."}]}},"aube":{"discussions":{"nodes":[{"number":852,"title":"`mise use -g aube` fails with GitHub artifact attestation verification failed","url":"https://github.com/aubepkg/aube/discussions/852","updatedAt":"2026-09-07T16:25:52Z","bodyText":"❯ mise use -g aube

visit aube.sh"},{"number":1413,"title":"Guidance on jsii@5.9.53 and fastq@1.20.2 trust downgrades in a transitive install","url":"https://github.com/aubepkg/aube/discussions/1413","updatedAt":"2026-08-29T12:42:55Z","bodyText":"Context
A cold aube install of the current cdktn-cli@0.24.0 dependency graph is blocked by two successive trustPolicy=no-downgrade decisions:

jsii@5.9.53 has an SLSA provenance attestation, but an earlier release (5.9.18) used the stronger trusted-publisher path.
After narrowly excluding that version to continue the audit, fastq@1.20.2 has no trust evidence, while 1.20.0 and 1.20.1 used the trusted-publisher path and carried provenance.

The policy results look correct according to Aube's documented evidence ranking. I am asking for guidance on the intended disposition: whether either release should become a reviewed exact built-in exception, or whether both should remain user-local exceptions pending confirmation from their upstream maintainers.
Minimal reproduction
With Aube 2.2.0 on Linux x64, create:
{
  "name": "aube-trust-repro",
  "private": true,
  "dependencies": {
    "cdktn-cli": "0.24.0"
  }
}
Then resolve without materializing node_modules:
$ aube install --lockfile-only --reporter append-only
ERR_AUBE_TRUST_DOWNGRADE

trust downgrade for jsii@5.9.53 (trustPolicy=no-downgrade): earlier
published version 5.9.18 had trusted publisher but this version has
provenance attestation
Apply only the exact exception needed to continue resolution:
$ NPM_CONFIG_TRUST_POLICY_EXCLUDE='jsii@5.9.53' \
    aube install --lockfile-only --reporter append-only
ERR_AUBE_TRUST_DOWNGRADE

trust downgrade for fastq@1.20.2 (trustPolicy=no-downgrade): earlier
published version 1.20.0 had trusted publisher but this version has no
trust evidence
The direct checks agree and neither package currently has a built-in exception:
$ aube trust check jsii@5.9.53
jsii@5.9.53: downgrade
published: 2026-08-24T05:25:34.425Z
current evidence: provenance attestation
strongest earlier evidence: trusted publisher (5.9.18)

$ aube trust check fastq@1.20.2
fastq@1.20.2: downgrade
published: 2026-08-28T00:52:38.498Z
current evidence: none
strongest earlier evidence: trusted publisher (1.20.0)
Dependency path
The relevant path is ordinary semver resolution rather than an exotic dependency source:
cdktn-cli@0.24.0
├─ peer jsii@~5.9.0 -> jsii@5.9.53
└─ @cdktn/hcl2cdk@0.24.0
   └─ jsii-rosetta@~5.9.0
      └─ fast-glob@^3.3.3
         └─ @nodelib/fs.walk@^1.2.3
            └─ fastq@^1.6.0 -> fastq@1.20.2

This also means a package-level workaround on cdktn-cli is not a good fit: the publishers correctly use compatible ranges, and the evidence churn belongs to the transitive packages' release processes or Aube's reviewed exception policy.
Registry/source evidence reviewed
jsii@5.9.53

npm publisher metadata names aws-cdk-team <aws-cdk-dev@amazon.com> rather than the earlier GitHub Actions trusted publisher.
npm provides both its publish attestation and an SLSA provenance attestation.
The Sigstore certificate binds the SLSA statement to aws/jsii-compiler, .github/workflows/release.yml, tag v5.9.53, and commit 16812ce0195d2cd505dc1edef4efd1a08a63cf55.
The public repository has the matching v5.9.53 tag at that commit.

So this is a real rank downgrade under the current policy, but it retains CI-bound provenance rather than dropping to no evidence.
fastq@1.20.2

1.20.0 and 1.20.1 were published by GitHub Actions <npm-oidc-no-reply@github.com> and carry provenance attestations.
1.20.2 was published by matteo.collina <hello@matteocollina.com> and has no npm attestation endpoint.
npm's gitHead is 4cdcc374ad2f2a606686ab9c8c5cf9ebec05ec03, matching the public mcollina/fastq version-bump commit. That commit is unsigned.

This is the stronger case for leaving the block in place until upstream confirms the manual release was intentional.
Questions

For jsii@5.9.53, is an exact built-in exception appropriate once the tag/workflow provenance above is verified, or should trusted-publisher-to-provenance transitions always remain local exceptions?
For fastq@1.20.2, is the intended next step an upstream report rather than an Aube exception because the release dropped all structured evidence?
When a normal transitive graph reveals several independent downgrades serially, is there a recommended audit workflow beyond adding one temporary exact exclusion at a time and rerunning resolution?

Related policy/reproduction precedent: jdx/mise discussion #11374 and the aube trust check work released from #1144."},{"number":1405,"title":"Installed npm-backend tool trees and internal build-toolchain caches (e.g. node-gyp) are not invalidated across aube store-layout changes, and dangling symlinks are never detected or self-repaired","url":"https://github.com/aubepkg/aube/discussions/1405","updatedAt":"2026-08-29T00:33:37Z","bodyText":"Title
Installed npm-backend tool trees and internal build-toolchain caches (e.g. node-gyp) are not invalidated across aube store-layout changes, and dangling symlinks are never detected or self-repaired
Summary
aube (embedded in mise for npm:-prefixed tool installs) symlinks every installed tool's dependencies into a shared, aube-owned cache/store rather than giving each tool its own copy. When that store's on-disk layout or contents change — either because the store was manually cleared, or because aube itself changed its store scheme in a newer version — previously-installed tool trees keep symlinks pointing at the old layout. Those symlinks go dangling silently: nothing in aube or mise detects this, there is no repair-on-detect, and the first symptom a user sees is an unrelated tool crashing with MODULE_NOT_FOUND at runtime, often much later and out of context from whatever caused the store to change.
This has happened twice independently on the same machine:
Incident 1 — shared store deletion breaks 12 unrelated tools (2026-08-04)
During unrelated debugging, ~/.cache/aube/virtual-store/ was deleted (the then-current global virtual store path). This produced 395 dangling symlinks across 12 installed npm: tools (claude-smart, adhd-agent, aislop, claude-code-analytics, claude-code-ultimate-guide-mcp, claude-multiprofile, claudecto, @code-insights/cli, okfy-ai, pyright, tsup, typescript) — none of which were the tool being debugged. Each affected tool failed at runtime with Error: Cannot find module '.../node_modules/.mise/<pkg>@<version>/node_modules/<pkg>/bin/<pkg>.js' / MODULE_NOT_FOUND. The store had partially regenerated from one unrelated reinstall (322/717 entries), but the 395 entries needed by the other 12 tools were never regenerated on their own. Repair required a manual, per-tool mise install --force npm:<tool> for all 12 — there was no single command to detect or repair this in bulk, and no warning that it had happened.
Incident 2 — aube version bump (bundled in a mise upgrade) orphans an internal toolchain cache (2026-08-28)
node-gyp (aube's internal build-toolchain dependency, used to compile native modules like node-pty — not a user-declared npm: tool) was provisioned on 2026-08-21 under ~/.cache/aube/tools/node-gyp/v12/, with its node_modules/.mise/node-gyp@12.4.0 entry symlinked into ~/Library/Caches/mise/npm/aube/cache/virtual-store/v1/node-gyp@12.4.0-<hash>. Between then and 2026-08-28, mise (Homebrew-installed, currently 2026.8.14) updated its embedded aube/aube-registry dependencies (jdx/mise#11759 changed the npm-backend cache scheme from a global virtual store to a mise-owned, per-invocation cache/store pair; aube-registry v2.1.0, 2026-08-23, separately touched node-gyp shim handling). The new store layout on disk (.../aube/store/v1/{files,index}, content-addressed) has nothing at the old cache/virtual-store/v1/... path the pre-existing node-gyp install still referenced.
Result: any npm: install requiring a native-module build (npm install npm:@google/gemini-cli@latest, via its node-pty dependency) failed with:
Error: Cannot find module '/Users/.../.cache/aube/tools/node-gyp/v12/node_modules/.mise/node-gyp@12.4.0/node_modules/node-gyp/bin/node-gyp.js'

Repair: deleting only the stale ~/.cache/aube/tools/node-gyp tree (not the shared store) and re-running the install let aube re-provision node-gyp fresh against the current store. This worked, but nothing surfaced why it broke or that it was safe to do — that required manual investigation of aube's own source/changelog to distinguish "delete this tool's own tree" (safe) from "delete the shared store" (the exact mistake from Incident 1).
Why this matters

No detection. Neither mise doctor nor any aube/mise command flags a dangling .mise symlink. It's discovered only when something tries to require()/import through it, often for a tool with no relation to whatever caused the store to change.
No repair-on-detect. Even once found, repair is a manual per-tool mise install --force npm:<tool> (or, for an aube-internal dependency like node-gyp that isn't a user-declared tool at all, manually deleting its private tree) — there's no single command that scans installed trees and re-links or reinstalls whatever's broken.
The blast radius is invisible from the trigger. In both incidents, the action that caused the breakage (a manual rm -rf in one case, an ordinary mise/Homebrew upgrade in the other) gave no indication that other, unrelated tools were now broken. A user has to independently discover and diagnose each one.
Version bumps to aube's own store layout don't migrate or invalidate old installs. Incident 2 specifically shows that even without any user action, an aube version change bundled into a routine mise upgrade can silently orphan a previously-working, aube-managed internal cache.

Suggested fix (any of, ideally more than one)

On mise install/mise use/mise up for any npm: tool (and internally, whenever aube provisions its own dependencies like node-gyp), verify that the tool's node_modules/.mise/* symlinks resolve before trusting them; if any are dangling, treat it as "not installed" and reinstall automatically rather than surfacing a raw MODULE_NOT_FOUND from deep inside the tool's own runtime.
On an aube version bump that changes the store's on-disk layout/scheme, either migrate existing store references or proactively invalidate/re-link previously-installed trees so they get re-provisioned against the new layout on next use.
Add a mise doctor/aube-level check that scans installed npm:-backend tool trees (and aube's own internal toolchain directories) for dangling .mise symlinks and reports them, the way mise doctor already reports other classes of problems.

Environment

mise 2026.8.14 macos-arm64 (Homebrew-installed)
aube/aube-registry versions bundled per jdx/mise#11759 (aube 1.38.0+) and the 2026-08-23 aube-registry 2.1.0 update
macOS, arm64 (Apple Silicon)"},{"number":1398,"title":"`autoInstallPeers` differs from pnpm for importer peers, breaking lockfile interoperability","url":"https://github.com/aubepkg/aube/discussions/1398","updatedAt":"2026-08-28T12:42:02Z","bodyText":"Summary
Hi! I ran into what looks like a difference between Aube 2.2.0 and pnpm 11.24.0 around autoInstallPeers.
With the default autoInstallPeers: true, the two tools disagree about which automatically installed peers should appear in a workspace importer's dependencies, and the disagreement goes in both directions:


A dependency's peer is promoted into the importer by Aube.
Aube adds a peer required by one of the workspace package's dependencies to that workspace importer's dependencies, even though that specifier does not appear in the workspace package's manifest.


A peer declared by the workspace package itself is not installed by Aube.
If the workspace package itself declares a peerDependency, Aube leaves its importer empty and does not link that peer, while pnpm auto-installs it.


The second case is the one that looks most surprising to me. aube config explain autoInstallPeers describes the option as:

missing peer dependencies are auto-installed during resolution and hoisted into the importer

In case 2, the workspace package's own missing peer appears not to be handled by that rule.
The practical consequence is that lockfiles written by Aube and pnpm are rejected by the other tool under --frozen-lockfile. This makes it difficult to evaluate Aube as a reversible migration path from pnpm.
I also confirmed that the same importer shapes appear in Aube's native aube-lock.yaml, so this seems to originate in resolution / graph construction rather than only in the pnpm lockfile writer.
Minimal reproduction
There are four files and no initial lockfile.
package.json
{
  "name": "repro-root",
  "private": true,
  "version": "0.0.0"
}
pnpm-workspace.yaml
packages:
  - packages/*
packages/case-a/package.json
This package depends on another package that has a peer:
{
  "name": "case-a",
  "version": "0.0.0",
  "private": true,
  "dependencies": {
    "react-dom": "19.2.0"
  }
}
packages/case-b/package.json
This package declares a peer of its own:
{
  "name": "case-b",
  "version": "0.0.0",
  "private": true,
  "peerDependencies": {
    "react": "19.2.0"
  }
}
pnpm 11.24.0 result
The relevant importer entries are:
importers:
  packages/case-a:
    dependencies:
      react-dom:
        specifier: 19.2.0
        version: 19.2.0(react@19.2.0)

  packages/case-b:
    dependencies:
      react:
        specifier: 19.2.0
        version: 19.2.0
The resulting workspace links are:
packages/case-a/node_modules -> react-dom
packages/case-b/node_modules -> react

So pnpm uses React to satisfy react-dom's peer without adding React as a manifest dependency of case-a, while the peer declared directly by case-b is auto-installed into that importer.
Aube 2.2.0 result
Aube produces:
importers:
  packages/case-a:
    dependencies:
      react:
        specifier: ^19.2.0
        version: 19.2.0
      react-dom:
        specifier: 19.2.0
        version: 19.2.0(react@19.2.0)

  packages/case-b: {}
The resulting links are:
packages/case-a/node_modules -> react react-dom
packages/case-b/node_modules -> (empty)

The interesting parts are:

react@^19.2.0 is added to case-a even though that specifier appears in no project manifest.
case-b declares react@19.2.0 as its own peer, but React is not installed or linked there.

Frozen-lockfile interoperability
Each tool accepts the lockfile it generated itself.
However, using the other tool's lockfile fails in both directions.
pnpm reading Aube's lockfile
$ pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

ERR_PNPM_OUTDATED_LOCKFILE
specifiers in the lockfile don't match specifiers in package.json:
* 1 dependencies were removed: react@^19.2.0

Aube reading pnpm's lockfile
$ aube install --frozen-lockfile

× lockfile is out of date with package.json:
  packages/case-b: manifest removed react

So this is not just a serialization difference: the two resolvers have different ideas about what belongs in the importer.
Expected / question
I'm not completely sure what behavior Aube intends for case A, so I would be interested in your view there.
For case B, I would expect a peer declared by the workspace package itself to be auto-installed when autoInstallPeers is enabled, consistent with the current configuration description.
If matching pnpm's importer semantics is also an intended compatibility goal, resolving both differences would have the additional benefit of making an Aube trial on an existing pnpm repository much easier to roll back without rewriting the lockfile.
Two related observations
I noticed two smaller things while investigating this. They may be unrelated, so I'm happy to open separate discussions if that is preferable.
1. strict-peer-dependencies=true
With case B, enabling:
strict-peer-dependencies: true
does not seem to report the missing peer. The peer remains uninstalled, but no strict-peer error is emitted.
2. aube check on a damaged install tree
On one Linux x64 run, aube install exited successfully while leaving:
packages/<pkg>/node_modules/argon2

as a dangling symlink, with the corresponding:
node_modules/.aube/argon2@0.45.1/

directory absent.
A second install repaired the tree, and I have not been able to reproduce the original install failure, so I do not have a reliable repro for that part.
What was reproducible once the tree was in that state was the diagnostic difference:

aube doctor correctly reported the install tree as stale.
aube check reported:

node_modules symlink tree is consistent (checked 0 packages)

So aube check gave a successful consistency result while checking zero packages, despite the dangling symlink.
Again, happy to split this into a separate discussion if useful.
Versions
Aube: 2.2.0
pnpm: 11.24.0
Node.js: 24.20.0
Platforms tested:
- macOS arm64
- Linux x64

Thanks for taking a look. Aube otherwise worked impressively well on the larger repository where I found this — dependency resolution, patches, native packages, TypeScript tooling, and cross-platform lockfile generation were all very close to pnpm — so I wanted to reduce this down to a small reproduction before reporting it."},{"number":1343,"title":"aube writes `catalog:` into `pnpm-lock.yaml` overrides and importer specifiers","url":"https://github.com/aubepkg/aube/discussions/1343","updatedAt":"2026-08-28T00:27:12Z","bodyText":"aube: 1.41.0 linux-x64 (2026-08-16)
pnpm: 11.22.0 (CLI reports 11.10.0 for the same binary)
OS: Linux x64
Case: https://github.com/mwolson/tmp-aube-issues/tree/main/pnpm-catalog-override-lock-write
Script: https://github.com/mwolson/tmp-aube-issues/blob/main/pnpm-catalog-override-lock-write/repro.sh

pnpm 11 resolves catalog: before it writes pnpm-lock.yaml. With a workspace catalog of is-number: 7.0.0 and overrides: { is-number: "catalog:" }, a pnpm lockfile stores:
overrides:
  is-number: 7.0.0
and the importer records specifier: 7.0.0, even though package.json still says "is-number": "catalog:".
#249 already taught aube to read that shape, so aube install --frozen-lockfile accepts a pnpm-written lockfile. The writer still emits the raw catalog: string. After aube add or a non-frozen aube install that rewrites the lock, official pnpm frozen CI dies:
ERR_PNPM_LOCKFILE_CONFIG_MISMATCH
The current "overrides" configuration doesn't match the value found in the lockfile

Restore only the overrides map to 7.0.0 and the next error is the importer specifier:
ERR_PNPM_OUTDATED_LOCKFILE
* 1 dependencies are mismatched:
  - is-number (lockfile: catalog:, manifest: 7.0.0)

aube frozen-installs its own rewrite. The lockfile is only toxic to real pnpm.
I hit this adding a single package in a catalog-heavy monorepo whose GitHub vp install uses official pnpm 11. Grafting the new package onto the previous pnpm-shaped lockfile made CI green again.
Reproduction
From the case directory, with PNPM_BIN or AUBESHIM_REAL_PNPM pointed at real pnpm:
git clone https://github.com/mwolson/tmp-aube-issues.git
cd tmp-aube-issues/pnpm-catalog-override-lock-write
./repro.sh
The script exits 1 on aube 1.41.0. It first lets pnpm write a green lockfile, then runs aube add --filter app is-odd@3.0.1, and checks both error layers. is-odd is only there to force a lockfile write. A non-frozen aube install after adding that dep to the manifest by hand does the same rewrite.
Equivalent by hand:
mkdir -p repro/packages/app && cd repro

cat > package.json <<'EOF'
{ "name": "catalog-override-lock-write", "private": true }
EOF

cat > pnpm-workspace.yaml <<'EOF'
packages:
  - "packages/*"

catalog:
  is-number: 7.0.0

overrides:
  is-number: "catalog:"
EOF

cat > packages/app/package.json <<'EOF'
{
  "name": "app",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "private": true,
  "devDependencies": {
    "is-number": "catalog:"
  }
}
EOF

# Real pnpm, not an aube/aubeshim shim.
CI=1 pnpm install --ignore-scripts --lockfile-only
CI=1 pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts   # ok

aube add --filter app is-odd@3.0.1 --ignore-scripts
CI=1 pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts   # LOCKFILE_CONFIG_MISMATCH
aube install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts        # ok
Expected
When aube writes pnpm-lock.yaml, emit the same catalog-resolved override value and importer specifier that pnpm writes, and that #249 already treats as fresh on the way in.
Related

#174 (the --frozen-lockfile rejects catalog: references in overrides comment)
#249 (read-path only: resolve catalog: when comparing, accept override-rewritten importer specs)"},{"number":1392,"title":"aube vs pnpm v12","url":"https://github.com/aubepkg/aube/discussions/1392","updatedAt":"2026-08-27T14:16:12Z","bodyText":"The recently released pnpm v12 has been rewritten in Rust and appears to offer improved performance.

https://www.npmjs.com/package/pnpm/v/12.0.0
https://github.com/pnpm/pacquet#benchmark
https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/releases/tag/v12.0.0
https://pnpm.io/blog/releases/12.0
https://pnpm.io/ja/blog/whats-different-in-pnpm-12

Note that https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/releases/latest is v11.24.0, not v12.0.0 for now.
The current benchmark in aube is based on pnpm v11.24.0 and it says about 6.1x faster than pnpm in Fresh install (warm cache).
Also, it appears that aube was ~1.9x faster than pacquet (pnpm v12) in a5d7462.
I'm curious to see which tool performs better at this point."},{"number":1342,"title":"Support Ubuntu Focal/Jammy with ARM64 GNU artifacts (glibc 2.31 baseline)","url":"https://github.com/aubepkg/aube/discussions/1342","updatedAt":"2026-08-23T18:19:20Z","bodyText":"The aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu artifact for Aube v1.41.0 appears to require symbols up to GLIBC_2.39. As a result, it does not run on:

Ubuntu Focal: glibc 2.31
Ubuntu Jammy: glibc 2.35

This affects ARM64 packaging runners using Focal or Jammy. The x86_64 GNU artifact does not appear to have the same compatibility problem.
Tests performed


The official v1.41.0 ARM64 GNU artifact failed on both Focal and Jammy.


Building with the existing older-glibc cross image, ghcr.io/cross-rs/aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu:0.2.5, produced an ARM64 binary requiring only GLIBC_2.18. It ran successfully on both distributions.


That cross image is amd64-only, however, so it cannot be used directly as a native ARM64 container.


A native ARM64 build using:
cargo zigbuild --release --locked \
  --target aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu.2.31 -p aube
produced a normal GNU binary requiring no newer than GLIBC_2.30. It ran successfully on ARM64 Focal and Jammy containers.


PGO and BOLT
I also adapted the PGO process to use cargo-zigbuild for every compilation phase. A custom linker wrapper handled the -u __llvm_profile_runtime argument that Zig otherwise interprets incorrectly.
PGO completed successfully and produced a compatible ARM64 GNU binary. BOLT did not:

Zig did not support the required --emit-relocs output.
llvm-bolt requires relocations for AArch64 instrumentation.
--allow-stripped did not resolve the issue.

Therefore, the resulting ARM64 build used PGO but not BOLT. Thin LTO was used because the test ARM64 machine had 8 GiB of RAM.
Benchmark
A hermetic install benchmark compared the official ARM64 v1.41.0 artifact, using the existing PGO/BOLT release path, with the ARM64 Zigbuild artifact using PGO but no BOLT:



Scenario
Official
Zigbuild PGO-only




Warm install
405.6 ± 97.3 ms
411.9 ± 47.8 ms


Cold install
13.230 ± 1.004 s
12.812 ± 0.745 s


Install + test
16.9 ± 2.5 ms
14.6 ± 1.7 ms



The results show little to no measurable difference for this workload, although the sample size was small and the builds were not identical: the Zigbuild artifact used thin LTO and no BOLT.
Important caveat: the benchmark ran on macOS using ARM64 Linux containers. It was not run on physical Focal or Jammy hosts.
Proposal
Could the ARM64 GNU release be built with a glibc 2.31-compatible baseline using either:

cargo-zigbuild --target aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu.2.31, including all PGO phases; or
A Focal or older ARM64 container/sysroot running on a real ARM64 host?

It would also be useful to add ARM64 Focal/Jammy runtime checks to release CI and leave ARM64 BOLT disabled unless relocatable output and a measurable performance benefit can be demonstrated."},{"number":1351,"title":"--disable-global-virtual-store parses but never applies the setting","url":"https://github.com/aubepkg/aube/discussions/1351","updatedAt":"2026-08-23T11:51:21Z","bodyText":"Summary
--disable-global-virtual-store is accepted by the CLI but does not resolve enableGlobalVirtualStore to false. node_modules/.aube/* entries stay absolute symlinks into the per-user store, in either argument position. Every other documented source of the setting works.
aube 1.41.0 (2026-08-16), linux x86_64.
Repro
mkdir repro && cd repro
cat > package.json <<'JSON'
{ "name": "repro", "private": true, "dependencies": { "nanoid": "6.0.1" } }
JSON
aube install          # create lockfile
rm -rf node_modules
aube ci --disable-global-virtual-store
ls -la node_modules/.aube/ | grep nanoid
Result:
nanoid@6.0.1 -> /home/user/.cache/aube/virtual-store/v1/nanoid@6.0.1-ed6f428285390c2b

Matrix



invocation
.aube entry

AUBE_ENABLE_GLOBAL_VIRTUAL_STORE=false aube ci
real directory

Same behavior with aube install in place of aube ci.
Expected
Per the enableGlobalVirtualStore docs in crates/aube-settings/settings.toml ("The global flags are one-shot CLI sources for the same setting: --disable-global-virtual-store resolves this setting to false"), the flag should force per-project materialization.
Impact

The env var is a working workaround."},{"number":497,"title":"`aube add` with a local path should suggest `file:` or `link:` prefixes instead of sending an HTTP request to npmjs","url":"https://github.com/aubepkg/aube/discussions/497","updatedAt":"2026-08-22T07:15:00Z","bodyText":"Consider a scenario where you want to test a locally developed library library-foo by loading it into another project project-bar.

Since package managers like pnpm and bun can handle local paths directly, it would be great if aube could handle them in the same way. Alternatively, if aube's policy strictly requires explicit prefixes (file:, link:), providing a friendly hint/suggestion in the error message would be very helpful."},{"number":1340,"title":"Peer-context fixed point never converges on a densely mutually-recursive peer graph (ERR_AUBE_PEER_CONTEXT_NOT_CONVERGED)","url":"https://github.com/aubepkg/aube/discussions/1340","updatedAt":"2026-08-20T18:46:17Z","bodyText":"Summary
aube add @deepseek-ai/dsh never reaches a peer-context fixed point and fails with ERR_AUBE_PEER_CONTEXT_NOT_CONVERGED.
npm resolves the same dependency graph without trouble, so the graph itself is satisfiable — the 16-iteration cap is what's being hit.
Reproduction
mkdir /tmp/t && cd /tmp/t && npm init -y
aube add @deepseek-ai/dsh@0.1.0-rc.7
█░░░░░░░░░░░░░░  428/1179 pkgs · resolving
ERROR aube_resolver::peer_context: peer-context hit MAX_ITERATIONS=16 without convergence code="ERR_AUBE_PEER_CONTEXT_NOT_CONVERGED" max_iterations=16
ERR_AUBE_PEER_CONTEXT_NOT_CONVERGED

  × failed to resolve dependencies
  ╰─▶ peer-context fixed-point did not converge after 16 iterations. mutually
      recursive peers, lockfile would be incomplete

Comparison with npm



resolver
result
package count




aube add
fails at iteration 16
climbs past ~1245 before aborting


npm install
succeeds in ~8 min
451 packages, 0 vulnerabilities



The package-count gap looks like the heart of it: npm flattens and dedupes, while aube duplicates per peer context to build the virtual store, so this graph's context count keeps growing instead of settling.
Why this graph is hard
@deepseek-ai/dsh has ~60 direct @deepseek-ai/dsh-* dependencies, and each of those declares peer dependencies on a dozen more siblings, which peer-depend back. For example @deepseek-ai/dsh-goal peer-depends on dsh-llm, dsh-agent, dsh-brand, dsh-scope, dsh-session, dsh-invariants, dsh-typert-protocol and dsh-session-projection, several of which peer-depend on dsh-goal's other peers in turn.
The sibling ranges are carets on prereleases (^0.1.0-rc.7), which resolve as >=0.1.0-rc.7 <0.2.0. Now that rc.6, rc.7 and rc.8 are all published, those ranges span three prereleases simultaneously across all ~60 packages.
This appears to be what tips it over rather than any single release: rc.6 installed successfully back when it was the newest prerelease, but re-resolving @deepseek-ai/dsh@0.1.0-rc.6 from scratch today fails identically. All of rc.6, rc.7 and rc.8 now fail the same way.
Workarounds tried, none effective
Each was set in an isolated project's .npmrc with node_modules and the lockfile removed in between; all four fail with the identical error.

auto-install-peers=false
dedupePeers=true
strict-peer-dependencies=false
peerDependencyRules.allowAny=true

MAX_ITERATIONS does not appear to be exposed as a setting, so there's no way to raise the cap for a graph that may simply need more iterations.
Suggestions
Making the iteration cap configurable would at least give an escape hatch for pathological graphs.
Beyond that, it would help to know whether this graph is genuinely non-convergent or merely slow to converge — the error reports the cap but not whether the context set was still changing when it gave up, which would distinguish "needs more iterations" from a true cycle.
If it is a true cycle, naming the mutually recursive packages in the diagnostic would make it actionable for the package author instead of a dead end for the user.
Environment

aube 1.41.0 linux-x64 (2026-08-16), invoked via mise 2026.8.9
Node v24.19.0
Linux 6.18.33.2-microsoft-standard-WSL2"},{"number":1333,"title":"pack does not resolve catalog: dependencies","url":"https://github.com/aubepkg/aube/discussions/1333","updatedAt":"2026-08-18T11:13:34Z","bodyText":"Summary
aube pack leaves catalog: dependency specifiers in the packed package.json, while pnpm 11.22.0 resolves them to concrete versions. This causes consumers such as @vscode/vsce to fail semver validation.
Reproduction
In a pnpm workspace containing a package with catalog dependencies:
{
  "devDependencies": {
    "@types/vscode": "catalog:",
    "@rspack/core": "catalog:"
  }
}
Run:
aube --dir path/to/package pack --pack-destination /tmp/aube-pack
pnpm --dir path/to/package pack --pack-destination /tmp/pnpm-pack
With aube 1.41.0, the packed manifest contains:
"@types/vscode": "catalog:"
With pnpm 11.22.0, it contains the resolved version, for example:
"@types/vscode": "1.105.0"
Both commands successfully create a tarball. The difference is only in the packed manifest.
Context
The project uses pnpm-workspace.yaml with a default catalog. The same behavior occurs when invoking pnpm through the aube shim; the shim resolves to aube 1.41.0.
Official aube documentation describes aube pack as matching pnpm pack, and pnpm documents replacing catalog: during pack/publish. Could you confirm whether this is a known limitation or bug, and whether catalog resolution is intended to be supported by aube pack?
Environment

aube 1.41.0
pnpm 11.22.0
macOS arm64"},{"number":1298,"title":"Isolated GVS keeps a stale nested identity for a patched dependency","url":"https://github.com/aubepkg/aube/discussions/1298","updatedAt":"2026-08-17T19:15:54Z","bodyText":"Repro repo: https://github.com/mwolson/tmp-aube-issues
Repro case: isolated-patched-gvs-stale-identity
aube version: 1.40.0 linux-x64 (2026-08-13)
Node version: v24.19.0
pnpm comparison: 11.21.0 isolated

Summary
Isolated aube with the default-on global virtual store can leave a third-party package's sibling node_modules/<dep> pointing at a different store identity than the project importer. A warm aube install does not rewrite that nested GVS link. --disable-global-virtual-store does.
I first hit this with a workspace-level patchedDependencies entry for effect@4.0.0-beta.103. The project resolved effect@4.0.0-beta.103-<hash> while @effect/platform-node's GVS instance still linked effect@4.0.0-beta.103_patch_hash=.... The bytes were the same. The realpaths were not. Rolldown inlined both copies, Effect's pre-response WeakMap split, and packaged desktop GET/POST responses lost Access-Control-Allow-Origin.
Expected
After aube install --node-linker=isolated, every importer of a patched is-number@7.0.0 resolves one package-root realpath. A later warm install should repair a stale nested GVS sibling link.
Actual
A fresh install is unified. If only the isolated sibling link under to-regex-range's GVS instance is pointed at a second store identity, a warm install leaves the split in place.
from app            .../is-number@7.0.0-<hash>/node_modules/is-number
from to-regex-range .../is-number@7.0.0-<hash>-stale-identity/node_modules/is-number
same realpath       false

--disable-global-virtual-store repairs the same retarget. Native pnpm 11.21.0 isolated keeps one is-number@7.0.0_patch_hash=... identity for both importers.
Repro
git clone https://github.com/mwolson/tmp-aube-issues
cd tmp-aube-issues/isolated-patched-gvs-stale-identity
./repro.sh
repro.sh exits non-zero when the issue is present. It uses a private AUBE_GLOBAL_VIRTUAL_STORE_DIR so it does not touch the user GVS.
Related

#1242 (hoisted same-version realpaths; fixed in 1.38.1)
#1293 (hoisted React peer nesting)
#1294 (Metro cannot resolve GVS realpaths)"},{"number":1294,"title":"Metro cannot resolve packages whose realpath is in the global virtual store","url":"https://github.com/aubepkg/aube/discussions/1294","updatedAt":"2026-08-17T19:15:53Z","bodyText":"Repro repo: https://github.com/mwolson/tmp-aube-issues
Repro case: metro-gvs-package-resolve
aube version: 1.40.0 linux-x64 (2026-08-13)
Node version: v24.19.0
Metro version: 0.84.4
pnpm comparison: 11.21.0

Summary
Isolated aube with the default-on global virtual store links node_modules/<pkg> to $XDG_CACHE_HOME/aube/virtual-store/.... Node resolves that package. Metro 0.84.4 does not.
I first hit this in an Expo 56 app as Unable to resolve "expo/virtual/env" after babel-preset-expo injected that import. The reduced case does not need Expo. Metro fails on is-number itself once the package realpath is outside projectRoot / watchFolders.
This looks like the same GVS incompatibility that disableGlobalVirtualStoreForPackages already handles for next, nuxt, vite, vitepress, and parcel. metro, expo, and react-native are not on that list.
Expected
After aube install --node-linker=isolated --enable-global-virtual-store, Metro.buildGraph resolves is-number the same way Node does.
Actual
Node resolves the package through the GVS realpath. Metro reports:
Unable to resolve module is-number from .../index.js: is-number could not be found within the project or in these directories:
  node_modules

Pointing resolver.extraNodeModules.is-number at the GVS realpath makes Metro list that path and still fail. Adding the same realpath to watchFolders makes Metro succeed.
Repro
git clone https://github.com/mwolson/tmp-aube-issues
cd tmp-aube-issues/metro-gvs-package-resolve
./repro.sh
repro.sh exits non-zero when the issue is present. It also checks the comparisons below and treats unexpected comparison failures as setup errors.
Comparisons

aube install --node-linker=isolated --disable-global-virtual-store: realpath stays under node_modules/.aube/. Metro succeeds.
AUBE_NODE_LINKER=hoisted aube install: hoisted mode writes a real node_modules/is-number directory. Metro succeeds.
Native pnpm 11.21.0 isolated: realpath stays under node_modules/.pnpm/. Metro succeeds.
Native pnpm with enableGlobalVirtualStore=true: realpath leaves the project and Metro fails the same way.

So this is Metro's file map plus a virtual store that lives outside the project. aube turns that store on by default for local isolated installs. pnpm leaves it off.
aubeshim is not required. I reproduced with aube directly.
Docs I checked

https://aube.jdx.dev/package-manager/global-virtual-store
https://aube.jdx.dev/package-manager/node-modules
https://aube.jdx.dev/troubleshooting
https://metrobundler.dev/docs/configuration/#watchfolders

Metro's own note: symlink targets inside watchFolders must also be inside watchFolders.
Related aube work: #32 and #101 added the auto-disable list. #117 later dropped names that had no concrete walk-up repro. #754 is isolated config-loader resolution, not this file-map miss.
Ask
Please add expo, react-native, and metro to the default disableGlobalVirtualStoreForPackages list.
The matcher is exact and only looks at direct dependencies. A typical Expo app declares expo and react-native, not metro. metro still belongs on the list for apps that depend on it directly.
Until then, enableGlobalVirtualStore=false or node-linker=hoisted keeps the realpath inside the project. A Metro watchFolders entry for the GVS realpath also works, but those store paths are content-hashed and change between installs, so they are awkward to keep in metro.config.js."},{"number":1293,"title":"Hoisted workspace materializes the same React version twice when an earlier importer pins another version","url":"https://github.com/aubepkg/aube/discussions/1293","updatedAt":"2026-08-17T19:15:52Z","bodyText":"Repo: jdx/aube
Category: Troubleshooting and Bugs
Observed: aube 1.40.0 linux-x64 (2026-08-13)
Compared with: native pnpm 11.21.0 and 10.24.0, Node v24.19.0, Linux x86_64
Related but distinct: #1242 hoisted-shared-realpath / #1243 share hoisted deps (same version across importers now shares a root placement). #1292 hoisted-auto-install-freshness is a different freshness-check issue and is not this report.
Case: https://github.com/mwolson/tmp-aube-issues/tree/main/hoisted-react-peer-duplication

Summary
In a two-importer workspace under node-linker=hoisted, aube lets the alphabetically earlier importer claim the workspace-root react slot. A later importer that pins a different React version, plus a hoisted peer-dependent package resolved in that later importer's peer context, then get two distinct react@<later> package-root realpaths. Node loads two module identities of the same version. Native pnpm hoisted places the later version once at the workspace root and nests only the earlier pin.
This is not explained by incompatible peer ranges. zustand@5.0.11 declares react: ">=18.0.0" (optional). Both 19.2.3 and 19.2.6 satisfy that range.
Minimal graph
Public packages only:

packages/mobile depends on react@19.2.3
packages/web depends on react@19.2.6 and zustand@5.0.11
workspace root has no React of its own

packages/mobile is earlier than packages/web in path order, which is what triggers aube's current root winner. Renaming the 19.2.3 importer to packages/zzz makes aube match pnpm.
Repro
https://github.com/mwolson/tmp-aube-issues/tree/main/hoisted-react-peer-duplication
git clone https://github.com/mwolson/tmp-aube-issues.git
cd tmp-aube-issues/hoisted-react-peer-duplication
./repro.sh
The script exits 0 when web and zustand resolve to the same react package-root realpath, and 1 when they do not. Isolated is the setup control and passes. Hoisted fails on aube 1.40.0.
Direct commands:
aube install --node-linker=isolated --ignore-scripts
# web and zustand both resolve to node_modules/.aube/react@19.2.6/...  (same realpath)

aube install --node-linker=hoisted --ignore-scripts
# web    -> packages/web/node_modules/react                 (19.2.6)
# zustand -> node_modules/zustand/node_modules/react        (19.2.6)
# mobile -> node_modules/react                              (19.2.3)
Aube 1.40.0 hoisted placements
From node_modules/.aube-state/hoisted-placements.json:
{
  "react@19.2.3": ["node_modules/react"],
  "react@19.2.6": [
    "packages/web/node_modules/react",
    "node_modules/zustand/node_modules/react"
  ],
  "zustand@5.0.11(react@19.2.6)": ["node_modules/zustand"]
}
require("react") from packages/web and from node_modules/zustand returns different module exports. Isolated aube on the same manifests returns the same export.
Native pnpm hoisted (nodeLinker: hoisted)
pnpm 11.21.0 node_modules/.modules.yaml:
{
  "nodeLinker": "hoisted",
  "hoistedLocations": {
    "react@19.2.6": ["node_modules/react"],
    "react@19.2.3": ["packages/mobile/node_modules/react"],
    "zustand@5.0.11(react@19.2.6)": ["node_modules/zustand"]
  }
}
pnpm 10.24.0 records the same locations. Web and zustand both resolve to the single root react@19.2.6 and share one module export.
Why this is not just "two React versions in one workspace"
Two exact React pins are an intentional workspace fact. Isolated aube already isolates them correctly: one react@19.2.6 identity for web plus zustand, and react@19.2.3 for mobile.
The hoisted failure is the extra split of react@19.2.6 into two package roots after 19.2.3 occupies the workspace root. #1243 share hoisted deps already says compatible dependencies should share one physical package at the root when they can, and that version or peer-context conflicts remain nested. Nesting 19.2.3 vs 19.2.6 is expected. Materializing 19.2.6 twice is the part that differs from pnpm and that produces two React identities in one web runtime.
Questions

When a version cannot occupy the workspace root, should every placement of that same version still share one package-root realpath?
Should the root winner prefer the version needed by more dependents or peer contexts, as pnpm does here, instead of the first importer in workspace order?
Is this in scope as a follow-up to #1243 share hoisted deps, or is first-importer-wins plus multiple nest directories considered supported hoisted semantics?"},{"number":1292,"title":"Hoisted workspace auto-install reinstalls on every command (`installed entry missing`)","url":"https://github.com/aubepkg/aube/discussions/1292","updatedAt":"2026-08-17T19:15:51Z","bodyText":"Repo / case: https://github.com/mwolson/tmp-aube-issues/tree/main/hoisted-workspace-auto-install-freshness
aube: 1.40.0 linux-x64 (2026-08-13)
Platform: Linux x64
Category: Troubleshooting and Bugs

Summary
After a valid hoisted workspace install, a member-only direct dependency is
placed at the workspace-root node_modules/<dep>. The package-local
packages/<pkg>/node_modules/<dep> slot is intentionally absent, Node
resolves through the root placement, and the same layout is what native
pnpm hoisted produces.
aube run and aube exec still treat that absent slot as
installed entry missing and perform another install on every invocation.
The next command sees the same valid hoisted layout and does it again.
Expected: a warm aube run after a fresh hoisted install.
Actual: every aube run prints Auto-installing: installed entry missing: packages/app/node_modules/is-number and reinstalls.
Minimal repro
The case is two importers (workspace root plus packages/app). Only
packages/app depends on public is-number@7.0.0. The workspace sets
nodeLinker: hoisted so follow-up commands stay hoisted without a shim.
git clone https://github.com/mwolson/tmp-aube-issues.git
cd tmp-aube-issues/hoisted-workspace-auto-install-freshness
./repro.sh; echo exit=$?
Exit 1 while the loop is present, 0 when aube stays warm.
The smallest direct commands, from that directory:
aube install --node-linker=hoisted --ignore-scripts
# Node resolves packages/app -> root node_modules/is-number
# packages/app/node_modules/is-number does not exist

aube run ok
aube run ok
AUBE_NO_AUTO_INSTALL=1 aube run ok
aube exec -c -- node -e "process.stdout.write('ok\\n')" hits the same
freshness check. If the workspace does not set nodeLinker: hoisted,
AUBE_NODE_LINKER=hoisted aube run ok is the equivalent form.
Observed on aube 1.40.0
Clean hoisted install:
root is-number exists: yes
package-local is-number exists: no
resolve from packages/app: .../node_modules/is-number/index.js
package realpath: .../node_modules/is-number

Then two consecutive aube run ok invocations, each:
Auto-installing: installed entry missing: packages/app/node_modules/is-number
dependencies:
+ is-number@7.0.0

aube 1.40.0 by jdx.dev · ✓ installed 1 package in 8ms
ok

The package-local path is still absent afterward, so the next command
repeats. AUBE_NO_AUTO_INSTALL=1 aube run ok prints only ok.
.aube-state records the importer-local path that the hoisted linker
never created. hoisted-placements.json has the real placement:
"direct_entries": {
  ".": [],
  "packages/app": ["packages/app/node_modules/is-number"]
}
{"is-number@7.0.0":["node_modules/is-number"]}
Why this matters
On a large hoisted workspace the same false stale check reinstalls the
whole tree on every script or exec. That turns cheap repeat commands into
multi-second or multi-tens-of-second installs, and it never converges
because the valid hoisted layout still lacks the package-local slot.
If a follow-up command does not keep node-linker=hoisted, the first
auto-install rewrites the tree to isolated and the second command stays
warm. The repeating loop is the hoisted-stays-hoisted case.
Related
This is a follow-on to the hoisted sharing fix, not a regression of the
shared-realpath identity bug:

#1242
#1243

In #1242, the maintainer confirmed that after the workspace-wide hoist,
packages/*/node_modules/<dep> is intentionally absent and importers
resolve upward to the root copy. Native pnpm 11.21.0 produces that same
root-only placement on this fixture.
The existence check itself comes from
#188 (warm-path direct_entries). I did
not find an existing discussion about this hoisted false-positive.
Docs

https://aube.jdx.dev/package-manager/install (auto-install before run/exec)
https://aube.jdx.dev/package-manager/node-modules (hoisted layout)
https://aube.jdx.dev/package-manager/workspaces
https://aube.jdx.dev/settings/#setting-nodelinker
https://aube.jdx.dev/settings/#setting-aubenoautoinstall"},{"number":1286,"title":"aube add re-resolves unrelated versions in a fresh npm package-lock.json","url":"https://github.com/aubepkg/aube/discussions/1286","updatedAt":"2026-08-17T19:15:50Z","bodyText":"Repo: https://github.com/mwolson/tmp-aube-issues
Case: npm-lock-add-reresolve
aube: 1.38.1 linux-x64 (2026-08-10)
Lockfile produced by: npm 11.17.0 install --ignore-scripts --package-lock-only --no-audit --no-fund
Same lock accepted byte-identical by npm 12.0.2

aube install treats a fresh npm package-lock.json as up to date. aube add of a named spec then re-resolves unrelated hoisted versions in that lock. Real npm only edits the named spec.
This is not the missing-entry repair in #690 npm-lock-missing-entry, the stale-lock-treated-fresh case in #964 lock-drift-fresh, or the optional-native recording in #938 npm-lock-optionals. After #1155 filter-add-optionals, the expected add lock diff was only the new package and its dependency.
Reproduction
git clone https://github.com/mwolson/tmp-aube-issues.git
cd tmp-aube-issues/npm-lock-add-reresolve
# Point NPM_BIN at a real npm if PATH npm is aubeshim.
./repro.sh
The script exits 1 while the issue is present.
Manual form of the same check:
cd npm-lock-add-reresolve

# Fresh: aube install leaves the lock's hoisted camelcase at 5.3.1.
aube install --ignore-scripts --reporter append-only

# Control: real npm only promotes the already-transitive is-number.
npm install is-number@7.0.0 --ignore-scripts --package-lock-only --no-audit --no-fund
# packages["node_modules/camelcase"].version is still 5.3.1

# Subject: aube add re-hoists camelcase.
aube add is-number@7.0.0 --ignore-scripts --reporter append-only
# packages["node_modules/camelcase"].version becomes 6.3.0
package.json pins jest-config at exact 29.7.0, matching the lock. npm hoists camelcase@5.3.1 (@istanbuljs/load-nyc-config wants ^5.3.1) and nests camelcase@6.3.0 under jest-validate (^6.2.0). is-number@7.0.0 is already a transitive.
The same 5.3.1 -> 6.3.0 hoist happens for:

aube add jest-config@29.7.0 (already the exact pin; manifest stays 29.7.0)
aube install --fix-lockfile (no named package)
isolated or hoisted AUBE_NODE_LINKER

--prefer-frozen-lockfile on add does not prevent it.
Smaller public trees did not reproduce the unrelated hoist: express@4.18.2, esbuild@0.25.12 (that case only strips optional: true from platform packages), and a two-package @istanbuljs/load-nyc-config@1.1.0 + jest-validate@29.7.0 pair.
Expected
aube add is-number@7.0.0 updates the is-number spec and keeps already-locked versions that still satisfy their ranges, the same way real npm install is-number@7.0.0 does. aube install --fix-lockfile should not rewrite a lock that aube install already treats as fresh.
Actual
aube add re-resolves the hoisted camelcase from 5.3.1 to 6.3.0. On a larger npm-accepted Expo lock the same path dropped optional and peer entries and changed dozens of unrelated top-level versions, including some that moved backwards.
Docs
https://aube.jdx.dev/package-manager/install.html (prefer-frozen reuses a fresh lock; --fix-lockfile repairs drifted entries)
https://aube.jdx.dev/package-manager/lockfiles.html
https://aube.jdx.dev/package-manager/dependencies.html"},{"number":1320,"title":"feat(store): add structured store-prune previews for automation","url":"https://github.com/aubepkg/aube/discussions/1320","updatedAt":"2026-08-17T15:20:16Z","bodyText":"Depends on — complete store-prune serialization with every CAS/index writer.
Concrete consumer — tw93/Mole#1421

Problem
aube store prune --dry-run doesn't give automated cleanup enough information
to act safely. It omits paths the real prune may change and doesn't report the
total space it could free.

aube store path prints only <storeDir>/v1, but prune also mutates the GVS
and opening Store can migrate <cacheDir>/index. See
store.rs,
gvs_registry.rs, and
aube-store/src/lib.rs.
GVS dry-run locking can create .prune.lock, so preview also needs the full
writer-exclusion protocol. See
gvs_registry.rs.
Human dry-run omits GVS bytes, a combined estimate, and structured paths.
aube doctor --json reports paths but also runs unrelated health checks. See
store.rs and
doctor.rs.

Proposal
Add JSON output to the existing preview.
aube store prune --dry-run --json
The output should include

every mutation root with an absolute path and kind
planned actions such as legacy index migration
GVS entries and bytes, CAS files and bytes, and stale project-record count
combined reclaimable bytes
structured warnings

Byte fields must identify upper bounds and avoid obvious hardlink double
counting.
Requirements

Root resolution matches real prune for configured, environment, workspace,
XDG, relative, ~, and relevant symlink paths.
Every new mutation root also appears in JSON output.
Preview doesn't delete, migrate the legacy index, initialize .projects, or
make another persistent layout change.
The complete prune/writer exclusion protocol protects one candidate snapshot.
JSON mode emits one document on stdout without progress or human text.
Failure doesn't delete anything, exits nonzero, and uses Aube's normal codes.

Example
Scheduled jobs could prune shared build runners or managed developer machines
only above a size threshold. disk cleaners like Mole could also validate every root before running
the serialized prune and skip cleanup when preview fails.

Like docs state:

On install (and on add, remove, update, dedupe), aube picks the lockfile to write from whichever supported file already exists in the project directory. Precedence is: aube-lock.yaml → pnpm-lock.yaml → bun.lock → yarn.lock → npm-shrinkwrap.json → package-lock.json. When none of those exist yet, aube writes aube-lock.yaml.

But if I have lock file drift and run aube clean --lockfile (nukes the lock file) followed by aube install, it creates aube-lock.yaml. And now I have aube-lock.yaml and pnpm-workspace.yaml.
For compatibility reasons with other tools I'd sometimes liked to keep using pnpm-lock.yaml."},{"number":1263,"title":"Aube doesn't error on `devEngines.packageManager.version` mismatch","url":"https://github.com/aubepkg/aube/discussions/1263","updatedAt":"2026-08-11T17:25:56Z","bodyText":"If I have aube@1.38.0 installed and I've defined devEngines in my project's package.json with a different version:
